questions.question: A simple way to make your motorcycle easier to see is to:

options.text: Ride with a large flag attached to its frame.
Ride with the headlight turned on.
Ride on the shoulder whenever possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride with the headlight turned on.
questions.explanation: Wear bright, reflective clothing to be more visible. Always ride with your headlight on. Use your turn signals and brake light when needed.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: Mirror checks:

options.text: Should only be done on long trips.
Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
Are not helpful since you can't do anything about what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often as part of your regular scanning. Always check your mirrors before changing lanes, at intersections, and before slowing down.

questions.question: Smoothly downshifting on motorcycles:

options.text: Can allow the rider to engine brake.
Should not be done if other vehicles are around.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can allow the rider to engine brake.
questions.explanation: Engine braking by downshifting smoothly can help you slow down. Use your brake lights separately so other drivers know you are slowing down.

questions.question: Common drugs, such as cold tablets:

options.text: Can affect a rider's abilities to safely operate their motorcycle.
Usually won't affect a rider's abilities to safely operate their motorcycle.
Pose no risk to a rider's operating abilities.
Are always acceptable to take before riding because they are sold over-the-counter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can affect a rider's abilities to safely operate their motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Most drugs, including over-the-counter medications, can affect your ability to ride safely. Learn about side effects before taking any drug and riding.

questions.question: Locking your brakes can:
questions.explanation: Locked brakes can cause control problems. If your front brake locks, release it and re-apply it quickly. If your rear brake locks on good pavement, keep it locked until you stop.

questions.question: To provide the best protection, a helmet should:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets DOT and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around with no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: When looking for a protective jacket or pair of pants, you should look for:
questions.explanation: Wear long pants and a jacket to cover your arms and legs while riding. Leather clothing provides the best protection.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Travel on the shoulder so you are not next to other traffic.

questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes when needed, slow down, and avoid sudden movements. Watch for oily areas, shaded spots, dirt, gravel, and bridges—they have less grip.

questions.question: Slippery surfaces can make it difficult to control a motorcycle. Which of the following would be considered a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers are slippery surfaces. Ride with extra caution on these surfaces.

questions.question: Which surface does NOT have poor traction?
questions.explanation: Many surfaces reduce tire traction. Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, and painted lane markings are all hazardous. Dry pavement is the safest surface for motorcycles.

questions.question: As a motorcycle rider, how can you help others see you?
questions.explanation: To be more visible, wear bright colors, keep your headlight on at all times, and always use your turn signals.

questions.question: What is usually in the center of a traffic lane?
questions.explanation: Oil and grease from cars collect in the center of lanes. On dry roads, this is usually safe for motorcycles. On wet roads, it becomes slippery.

questions.question: What do goggles protect when riding?

options.text: Your eyes, but not the rest of your face.
Your face, but not your eyes.
Your eyes as well as eyeglasses do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your eyes, but not the rest of your face.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes only. A face shield protects both your eyes and face. Regular eyeglasses do not provide enough protection.

questions.question: What does a face shield do?

options.text: Does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, impact-resistant face shield gives the best protection for your eyes and face. Eyeglasses or sunglasses are not enough. In Vermont, you do not need eye or face protection if your motorcycle has a windshield, but it is still recommended.

questions.question: Most crashes happen in daylight. How should you be more visible?
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen in daylight. Always wear bright colors while riding, even during the day.

questions.question: Which is NOT protective clothing for a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Protective clothing includes sturdy pants and jackets that cover your arms and legs, boots that support your ankles, and sturdy gloves. A stocking cap does not meet these requirements.

questions.question: When should a rider check their mirrors?

options.text: When slowing down or stopping suddenly

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors when slowing down, stopping, waiting at intersections, changing lanes, and turning.

questions.question: The body gets rid of about how much alcohol per hour?
questions.explanation: The body can eliminate about one drink per hour on average.

questions.question: What must you have to carry a passenger on a motorcycle?

options.text: A seat large enough for two riders.
You should not tell the passenger to wear protective clothing.
A sticker on the brake light to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: A seat large enough for two riders.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle must have a seat for two riders. It should also have footrests for the passenger. Your passenger should wear the same protective gear you wear.

questions.question: Shifting into a lower gear has a similar effect to:
questions.explanation: Shifting into a lower gear slows your motorcycle like using the brakes. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They warn drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: If a driver is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Move to one side of your lane to allow them to share the lane.

questions.explanation: The safest response is to let them pass. Change lanes when safe and let them go ahead. Speeding up will only make things more dangerous.

questions.question: Which type of material provides the best protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather clothing provides the best protection for motorcycle riders. Always wear clothing that covers your arms and legs completely when riding.

questions.question: The Motorcycle Safety Foundation teaches the SEE strategy for safe riding. What does "SEE" stand for?
questions.explanation: The SEE strategy helps riders make safe decisions. "SEE" stands for Search, Evaluate, and Execute.
